rv.q: The musical adaptation of Anne Rice's vampire chronicles is a bloodless affair that fails to capture the gothic romance of its source material.
It’s the absence of more lurid or even fresh imagination that makes this lethargic vampire tale fatally dull.
Despite those Rice credentials, the homoerotic / Oedipal potential and a score by the still-golden duo of Elton John and Bernie Taupin, the show is dim, dumb and dreary.
Dare to look upon "Lestat" and keep your eyelids from growing heavier and heavier and heavier.
The mediocrity of 'Lestat' might be an obstacle for the average theatergoer, but it should provide none for fans of Elton and Rice.
That would mean that the woeful Lestat, which just opened at the Palace, is truly the silver nail in the coffin of vampire musicals that it deserves to be.
Despite their heroic efforts, Menken and the rest of his creative team never shake the feeling of familiarity and predictability that plagues every scene.

cn.t: Critics savage this Elton John-Bernie Taupin vampire musical as lifeless and dull, with one memorably calling it a "musical sleeping pill." Despite the brand-name talent, the show fails to capture the gothic romance of Anne Rice's source material.
